justification: Adds six columns, a shape constraint and two triggers to regulatory_provisions in production and fills them for all 19,627 served council DCP rules. Nothing reads the columns yet (Phase C), so no served answer changes; not Critical. More than Minor because a wrong trigger would leave stale quotes once Phase C serves them.

pre_impl.existing_data: regulatory_provisions (new columns council_quote, quote_page, quote_source_path, quote_status, quote_reason, quote_checked_at); read: provision_text, pdf_page, source_council, source_chapter_key joined to dcp_chapter_registry.r2_current_path (dcp_page_repair.SERVED_SQL)
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: A rule edited between judging and writing: the UPDATE matches md5(provision_text) as judged, so the row keeps NULL and the final count shows it (stored N of M; exit 1).
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Existing served rows filled by `council_quote.py --apply`; rows changed later are cleared by trigger and need the copier re-run (Phase C wires it after every publish).

functions.name: judge
functions.input: served row + both readings of its chapter PDF
functions.output: dict with status, reason, council quote text and page

functions.name: write
functions.input: list of judge result dicts for every served rule
functions.output: UPDATE per chapter by id where md5(provision_text) matches
functions.if_none: no rows -> stores 0, exit 1 when fewer stored than judged

values.if_missing: exact/recovered without a quote is refused by the constraint

queries.where_clause: rp.id = v.id AND md5(rp.provision_text) = v.md5 AND rp.is_current
queries.if_wrong: id is the primary key; one row per value

break_it.scenario: A rule's text is edited after its quote was stored
break_it.what_happens: a stale 'exact' quote would describe text no longer stored
break_it.how: migration 111 regulatory_provisions_clear_quote nulls all six columns
break_it.repro: proven 2026-10-12 in a rolled-back transaction: id 150954 unconfirmed -> NULL after provision_text edit

break_it.scenario: The chapter gets a new PDF
break_it.what_happens: quotes copied from the old PDF stay
break_it.repro: UPDATE dcp_chapter_registry SET r2_current_path = ... in a transaction, then count quote_status IS NOT NULL for that chapter

break_it.scenario: A status says exact but no quote is stored
break_it.what_happens: Phase C would show nothing as the council's words
break_it.repro: proven 2026-10-12: UPDATE ... SET quote_status='exact' on id 150954 raised CheckViolation

break_it.scenario: Copy drops words or values from either end
break_it.what_happens: a partial control shown as the council's
break_it.how: council_quote.py judge: cut words must be page furniture else words_cut/values_cut

break_it.scenario: A rule's text is edited by an update that also stamps quote_checked_at, or a non-current row is later made current after its chapter got a new PDF
break_it.what_happens: a stale quote survives on the edited or revived rule
break_it.how: migration 112: any text/chapter change clears; a new PDF voids every row of the chapter
break_it.repro: PYTEST_REAL_DB=1 pytest -m database tests/test_council_quote_real_db.py -o addopts= -- both new tests failed (2 failed, 4 passed) before 112 was applied, 6 passed after

falsifiable_check.fails_when: a reworded quote is marked exact, a cut table row is recovered, an oversized row or an uncased line is passed as the council's text
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Before the cross-review fixes the label test expected 'recovered' for a copy with the unprinted ending 'as shown'; the stricter rule turned it red (1 failed, 9 passed) and the test was changed to expect words_cut.
falsifiable_check.external_authority: Production 2026-10-12 after --apply: served council rules by quote_status = exact 15,092 / recovered 1,431 / not_a_control 56 / unconfirmed 3,048; 0 not checked.
